Episode 259. The Truth of the World, Your Truth, My Truth (7)
"Heok!"
Valeria's eyes opened.
'A dream... was it a dream?'
She recalled the moment she had lost consciousness. While fighting, she had been c

aptivated by the illusion shown by Kelliark's desire, and in it, she had faced a future without pain. In a world where the Gray Owl Mercenaries didn't die, where people didn't die, she had felt happiness.
If it was a dream, she had never wanted to wake up. It was so vivid that she couldn't possibly think of it as a dream, and the harsh reality had instantly receded, leaving not even a trace.
But from some point on, painful things had suddenly started to come to mind.
The day she had realized Jin's death, the day Solderet had turned back time, and the days after that, when she had wandered endlessly through the pure white, desert-like dimensional passage.
It wasn't a dream.
[Valeria!?]
It was Luet. She, along with everyone else who had confirmed Valeria's corpse, was staring with wide eyes.
"Lady Luet..."

[You were definitely dead, how on earth... No, whatever the reason, I'm glad. Lani! Hurry and call Lani. Valeria needs to be healed enough to fight again so we can counter the manipulation even a little...!]
Valeria looked at Luet, trying to make sense of the flood of memories.
"I wasn't dead, my time was stopped..."
[What?]
"The moment a person who could be called my future... no, perhaps my past self, intervened in this world, my time was temporarily stopped."
She felt she could understand what had happened to her.
In that Solderet had turned back time, she was her future self; in that she had seen the records of the Demon Army from before he had turned back time, she was her past self.
It was confusing, but Valeria remembered the last words she had left for Jin. The present, the past, and the future are connected somewhere.
What was connecting us?
The desire to protect people, the feeling that she could not lose the world. For some reason, it felt like it was that. It felt like it could be nothing else.
Her wounds hurt.

She could feel pain from all over her torn and pierced body. It would hurt like death if even a single fingernail was pulled off, but the people fighting here had been enduring a pain incomparable to that for too long.
The smell of ash wafted in through the broken bridge glass. Explosions, and the screams and monstrous cries of people, and unknown, terrible sounds could be heard.
"How much time has passed since Jin left?"
[About ten minutes have passed.]
Only ten minutes.
In that time, countless people had died. Chiron and Van could no longer even attempt a counterattack, and most of the superhumans had been submerged in the red sea and had disappeared.
At least Hedo had reached the rank of a Genesis Knight and had defeated the Demon Army's Genesis Knights with Murakan, but now, the battles of humans were unlikely to have much meaning.
Because right after Jin had entered the legacy, the Origin Stone had been restored.

[Even that, we've held on thanks to the Patriarch and the Battle God resisting the manipulation. The two of them... are now being eroded by the manipulation. Valeria, you have to find the manipulated records.]
Murakan was forgetting Jin.
Hedo had forgotten Sandra, and Veradin and Dante had forgotten who each other were. Talaris had forgotten Syris, and Lucy had forgotten Haylin.
It was to the point where, among the remaining people, only about ten percent of them remembered the person named 'Jin Runcandel' on the battlefield now.

While history was being manipulated by the Origin Stone, they were just fighting blindly. Even as their memories blurred, only the determination to fight remained, and all they were doing was swinging their swords forward like the army of the abyss.
That sword was sometimes aimed not at Kelliark, but at each other.
No, it was often aimed at each other. In the first place, even before the Origin Stone had arrived, it was impossible to attack Kelliark unless one was a Genesis Knight.
Forgetting who Jin was, forgetting who they were, forgetting what they were fighting.
It wasn't just the battlefield.
The whole world was being manipulated that way. The 677th dimension, the starting point of all dimensions, was being submerged in crimson seawater, manipulated, and broken.

The battlefield was better, in a way. Thanks to the people who hadn't fallen yet, there were still people like Luet who were maintaining their consciousness here. Outside the battlefield, no such person was left.
"Now Jin... will be coming, Lady Luet."
[...The Young Patriarch!?]
"And he has not forgotten anything."
At that moment, from the middle of the red sea where Jin had disappeared, a single streak of pure white light shot up into the sky.
It was light.
Completely different from the golden sun energy that was illuminating Kelliark's entire body, a pillar of light as transparent and clear as water was splitting the sky.
Kelliark's gaze fell on that pillar.
He knew of the existence of the 'transcendent power' that Solderet had left in the legacy. But he didn't know exactly what it was.
The Origin Stone was restored anyway, and he had even taken the full power of the Sun God Kinzelo into his grasp. That meant there was nothing left in this world that could defy him.
'Jin Runcandel...'
Malugia, who had been hiding her power, Helluram, and the Vamel Alliance, who were enduring so tenaciously, were now all just waiting to be sunk into the red sea.
Kelliark had ultimately decided to destroy the 677th dimension without a trace. And when he unified all the dimensions into one, he would finally achieve what he had wanted.
It would be proof that he had obtained the power to change the unchangeable.
But why was the light bothering him? The absolute power he had just obtained was clearly a realm where he shouldn't even be able to feel such a thing.
[Be erased.]
Kelliark swiped at the air towards the pillar of light with the Origin Stone, which had turned into a staff. A space of tens of thousands of paces was torn like paper, but the light was not cut.
Unpleasant.

And, unsettling. He tried to erase the light with a stronger will once more, but the result was the same. On the contrary, while concentrating on the light, the manipulation that had been pressuring Chiron and Van was momentarily released.
"Ah... it seems your son has returned."
"He is your brother as well."
The moment the two opened their mouths, their consciousness hazy, Kelliark dropped a spear of the sun on their heads. There was no need to feel regret for them anymore.
Kiik!
The spear of the sun was being blocked by something. Naturally, Kelliark thought that the two had once again miraculously raised their swords and parried the spear.

But that wasn't it. The two giants had already created enough miracles. They no longer had the strength left to parry Kelliark's attacks. They hadn't even been aware of the fact that a spear made of solar energy had fallen on their heads.
What had blocked the spear was the light.
A flash occurred as if lightning had struck, and the spear of the sun was instantly cut into dozens of pieces and scattered.

Kelliark reflexively swung the Origin Stone. If they blocked the spear, all he had to do was perform more manipulation. He just had to distort the space they were in and completely crush their consciousness.
The disaster that was destroying the world momentarily stopped. Kelliark focused his authority to get rid of the two in front of Jin's eyes.

But this time too, the power of the Origin Stone seemed to be blocked by something and couldn't advance towards Chiron and Van. It just twisted and shimmered around them, but showed no signs of reaching them.
The moment he witnessed that scene, Kelliark suddenly remembered what had happened about ten minutes ago.
Really, can I kill him? Even if I become the one true god, can I truly annihilate Jin Runcandel?
It had been only about ten minutes ago. At that time, Kelliark hadn't been able to answer his own question, and the ominous premonition was approaching like reality.
'Are you saying... that the power Jin Runcandel obtained from the legacy is superior to the power of the Origin Stone and the Sun God?'
That couldn't be. Kelliark looked at the pillar of light again.
'It's gone?'
But the pillar had disappeared as if it were a lie, and Kelliark felt his heart pound like a human's and wrapped a shield around himself.
"Kelliark Zipple."
Light flashed once more.
Jin was already standing right in front of Kelliark. In Kelliark's eyes, he looked like a round ball of light. Regardless of its shape, he recognized that the light was Jin Runcandel.

But in the eyes of the people watching his back, he just looked like the Jin Runcandel they knew, the one they had forgotten until just now. It was Jin, holding his sword with a body full of wounds. It was the same appearance they knew so well.
[Hah?]
His neck was cut.

The moment Jin appeared in front of him, Kelliark knew that something sharp had cut his neck. He had created a manipulation to make it as if it hadn't happened, but the fact that he hadn't perceived the moment he was cut at all was a shock.
He had thought he had become the one true god.
No, he had been certain. Now, something he 'couldn't know' shouldn't be happening in the world. However, Kelliark was belatedly grasping what Jin's power was.
[Light? The light... was before even Kinzelo? Are you saying Solderet left that power to you?]
This time, his left arm fell off. Before Kelliark could attempt a manipulation, Jin cut the Origin Stone he held in his right hand, and then cut his neck again.
But Kelliark was standing behind Jin, looking perfectly fine. The Origin Stone also looked fine, as if it had never been cut.
[How absurd. To think that only Valeria Hister knew the truth of the world, that the beginning of everything was, in the end, light.]
Jin didn't care. He had known even before entering the legacy that the authority he had obtained was great.
He didn't think, the light I have obtained is superior to that. The only thing he could be sure of was that it was more righteous.

[Hmm... but what Solderet left you seems to be just a very small authority over light. Are you saying that's enough to fight me? Interesting, in many ways. I'll take that too. You should have just run away to another dimension. If you have that much power, you could have escaped from me for quite a long time. Do you have a lingering attachment to this world that is as good as destroyed? How very human.]
From the moment Jin had approached Kelliark, the people who had been submerged in manipulation and desire were waking up one by one. Kelliark couldn't easily submerge them again as before.
Soon, Jin aimed his sword at Kelliark and continued. Though in his eyes, it just looked like a round ball of light shaking slightly.
"Yes, Kelliark Zipple. Just like that... don't be afraid of me. Keep being certain that there is nothing left to be afraid of in the world. So that I can cut you down more easily."
